question: The slogan 'Aaram Haraam Hai' was given by______________.
solution:
The correct answer is Jawaharlal Nehru.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The slogan "Aaram Haraam Hai" was given by Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India.
 
• Nehru served as the **first Prime Minister from 1947** until he died in 1964, playing a crucial role in shaping modern India. 
 
• Nehru's notable works include:-
 
 
• **Towards freedom (Autobiography) (1936)**
 
• **The Discovery of India (1946) **
 
• **Glimpses of World History (1934).**
 
 
 
• Nehru became the **General Secretary** of the All India Congress Committee in September 1923.
 
• He was honored with the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award in **1955.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose:-**

 
 
• He founded the **Indian National Army** during World War II to fight against British colonial rule.
 
• Bose was initially a key member of the **Indian National Congress** and served as its **President **in **1938** but later resigned due to ideological differences.
 
• He declared the formation of the **Azad Hind Government in 1943 in Singapore**, proclaiming it as the provisional government of free India.
 
• He popularized the slogan **"Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!"** which inspired many Indians to join the freedom struggle.
 
• He is often referred to as** "Netaji" (meaning "Respected Leader").**
 
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh:-**
 
 
• He is known for his **radical approach** against British colonial rule.
 
• His slogan **'Inquilab Zindabad'**, meaning 'Long Live the Revolution', still resonates with many.
 
• Bhagat Singh** joined the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**, a revolutionary organization that aimed to overthrow British rule through armed struggle.
 
• On April 8, 1929, **Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt** threw non-lethal** bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly** to protest repressive laws, shouting slogans for revolution.
 
• Bhagat Singh was sentenced to death for the **murder of John Saunders**, a police officer, and was executed on March 23, 1931, along with Rajguru and Sukhdev.
 
 
 
• **Dayanand Saraswati:-**
 
 
• He founded the **Arya Samaj** in** 1875**.
 
• His slogan was **"Go back to the Vedas!"**.
 
• He authored** "Satyarth Prakash,"** which critiques religious dogmas and promotes rational thought.
 
• Dayanand strongly** opposed social evils** like caste discrimination, idol worship, and superstitions prevalent in society.
